[mot] in select areas that have $0 delivery, for me they are charging over $50 :(
[A Banana4scale] Anyone got any good healthy recipes. Most of the online recipes are very American biased and ingredients are all unavailable here
[cephh] literally just muscle nation custard casein vanilla protein powder with 98% skim milk thats all i use, i found sweetener to be personally repulsive and cant get passed half a pint with it in it, but without it i can smash it down
[eating kiwi fruit] Mate ignore all the people peddling special milks and pudding mixes. All the american recipes are useless for us here.
Here is my most recent choc high protein creami. Everything but the xanthan gum can be had at the big 2. I have the original machine, you might want to scale up for the ones with the larger tubs.
Wet:
300g light milk
3g vanilla extract
10g queen sugar free espresso topping (optional but makes the choc flavour awesome. I imagine some instant coffee might do the same job)
Dry:
30g choc protein powder (i use WPC. isolate is too watery. BN's protein matrix is awesome for this but I havent had any BN since price increases)
20g erythritol (can get at most big supermarkets now, often labeled as 'stevia' despite being mostly erythritol)
20g cocoa powder (use good dark cocoa. I imported mine as i find supermarket varieties to be quite hit or miss)
.5g salt
1g xanthan gum (will have to buy this one online)
Use a stick blender for the wet, and feed in the dry as it its running. I thaw for 10 mins on the kitchen bench, run lite ice cream program, and then mix in program.
If you want to feel loved, chuck a few oreos in for the mix in process. worth the calories.
[ASR-Briggs] Erythritol is really bad for you. All of the recent studies coming out are downright scary. Copy pasted from google:
• Blood Vessel Impairment in the Brain: Research published in the Journal of Applied Physiology shows that exposing human brain microvascular endothelial cells (the tiny blood vessels lining the brain) to typical beverage-equivalent amounts of erythritol increases cellular oxidative stress (free radicals) by roughly 75%.
• Reduced Nitric Oxide: Erythritol decreases the production of nitric oxide—a crucial compound that helps blood vessels relax and dilate—by about 20%, which can impair normal cerebral blood flow.
• Increased Endothelin-1: The sweetener raises the production of endothelin-1 (a potent vasoconstrictor that tightens blood vessels) by around 30%, shifting the balance toward constriction.
• Impaired Clot Dissolution: Erythritol blunts the release of tissue-type plasminogen activator (t-PA), a compound the body uses to break down blood clots, which elevates the risk of ischemic stroke and cerebrovascular events.
• Cognitive Decline and Memory Changes: A study featured by the American Academy of Neurology linked higher consumption of low- and no-calorie sweeteners—including erythritol, xylitol, sorbitol, aspartame, saccharin, and acesulfame-K—to faster declines in thinking and memory skills, an effect that researchers noted was particularly pronounced in individuals under age 60 or those with diabetes.
[eating kiwi fruit] Sorry mate, not going to bother refuting in-vitro slop & pointless mechanistic claims. Post human studies with proper control groups and stop letting bots think for you.
[ASR-Briggs] @eating kiwi fruit: "in-vitro slop & pointless mechanistic claims". You mean the standard studies done on any new ingredient BEFORE large scale human control group studies? Erythritol has only been mainstream since 2017. But you do you boo. I'll stick to aspartame, which isn't perfect, but has had thousands of studies done into it, and is one of the most researched food additives of all time.
[LurkMoar] @ASR-Briggs: erythritol is actually an excellent sweetener for frozen foods

[oatmatcha] Anyone with the deluxe think that any of the additional programs (frozen yogurt, creamiccino, slushi, italian ice, frozen drinks) make it worth getting the deluxe over this? I'm aware that the tub size is larger.

[Nortaggin] The 30% cashback deal is expired and is now 20%. Still a better deal than the $199(give or take a dollar or two) deal that amazon prime had. There's also the $10 off everyday market order code (still can't beat the 30% cashback though).
